sections.html:
Manhattan is a college and Army town, and that mix sets the tone for most home sales. The city is the seat of Riley County and reaches into Pottawatomie County. The 2020 census counted 54,100 people, up from 1,173 in 1870, and every census in between recorded growth.

Most owners compare an agent listing, a private sale and a cash offer. The local facts that tilt the choice are covered below: water and weather, rental rules, taxes and deed paperwork.

Manhattan lies in northeastern Kansas where the Big Blue River meets the Kansas River, about 50 miles west of Topeka. The original downtown was built on a broad, flat floodplain, and much of the city around it rolls into the Flint Hills. Tuttle Creek Reservoir is about five miles north, and the Konza Prairie preserve lies to the south.

Interstate 70 runs roughly nine miles south of the city, with three exits that feed Manhattan: K-177 at exit 313, McDowell Creek Road at exit 307 and K-18 at exit 303. US-24 crosses the city as Tuttle Creek Boulevard. Manhattan Regional Airport, on K-18 about two miles west of town, has American Eagle service to Chicago O'Hare and Dallas/Fort Worth, and the ATA Bus runs fixed routes inside the city.

sections.h2: Education and the Army drive demand
sections.html:
Manhattan began in 1855 with New England Free-State settlers, and the town took its name on June 29, 1855. Kansas State Agricultural College was established in 1863 and opened that September as the first public college in Kansas. The Kansas Pacific Railroad arrived in 1866.

Kansas State University employs more than 6,000 people on campus, more than anyone else in town. Other big names are Fort Riley, the National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility, Caterpillar Work Tools, USD 383 and Ascension hospital. Fort Riley's 100,656 acres lie between Manhattan and Junction City and are home to the 1st Infantry Division. Students, staff and soldiers keep a steady flow of renters and buyers moving through town.

Flood risk is the first environmental question many Manhattan buyers ask. The city was built at the downstream end of the Big Blue River watershed. The Big Blue and Kansas Rivers Floodplain Management Plan, sponsored by the Army Corps of Engineers, the State of Kansas, the city and both counties, describes the south and east side of the city as carrying a particular flood risk.

The plan counts 43 flood events between 1904 and 1951. The 1951 flood led to Tuttle Creek Dam, finished in 1962, and the Manhattan Levee System, finished in 1963. The city later raised the levee and replaced original equipment from the 1960s. The plan names residential areas along Casement Road and Marlatt Avenue as part of the studied floodplain, along with the commercial corridor on US-24 in Pottawatomie County.

What to do is straightforward. Look up your parcel's flood zone before talking price, check whether flood insurance is on the house, and collect any elevation certificate or repair records.

A humid continental climate keeps roofs, siding and heating systems busy. Yearly precipitation averages 35.77 inches. About 59 days reach 90 degrees or higher and about four fall to 0 degrees or lower. Snow averages 17.6 inches.

The most destructive tornado on record hit at about 10:30 p.m. on June 11, 2008. The EF4 storm destroyed 31 homes and caused about $20 million in damage on the Kansas State campus. An earlier tornado on June 8, 1966 injured at least 65 people. With storm damage on your house, choose between repairing it, disclosing it, and selling as is.

sections.h2: Rules for owners who rent a house
sections.html:
Under the city's rental registration program, owners register every rental unit. Inspections are not mandatory under the program, but the Risk Reduction office, at 785-587-4506, encourages owners to ask for one and offers a property maintenance checklist.

A house that has been a rental should be checked for registration before you sell, so no one raises it halfway through the deal.

  • Confirm that every rental unit you own is registered with the city.
  • Keep leases, deposit records and any inspection results together for the buyer.
  • Call Risk Reduction if you are unsure whether a unit needs attention before a sale.

sections.h2: Property taxes and what happens at closing
sections.html:
Real estate taxes in Riley County are billed in arrears: December 20 for the first half, May 10 of the following year for the second. A weekend December 20 pushes the deadline to the next business day. Visit the Treasurer's Office at 110 Courthouse Plaza in Manhattan, or pay by phone at 785-377-5385.

One assessment calendar covers the whole state. Valuation notices arrive by March 1, an equalization appeal must start within 30 days of mailing, and informal meetings with the appraiser run through May 15. A mid-year sale still leaves a bill for the year you are leaving, so ask the closing agent how it will be prorated.

Kansas requires a real estate sales validation questionnaire with almost every deed that is recorded. Under K.S.A. 79-1437c, the register of deeds cannot record a deed unless the questionnaire is attached, and the office keeps it for five years before destroying it.

Some transfers are exempt, including gifts, sheriff's deeds and transfers by an executor under court order, and the exemption number must be written on the document itself. Title companies normally prepare this paperwork, so a seller mostly needs to confirm that the price and the names on the deed are correct.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale compare with a listing?
sections.html:
A listing gives you the widest audience and the longest process: preparation, showings, buyer financing and the appraisal. A cash sale to a company like ours cuts out the lender, so the closing date is set by you and the title work, not by a loan file.

If your Manhattan house needs a roof, has water damage, carries tenants or came through an estate, price the as-is route next to a listing. The timeline depends on title work and on when you want to move. Call or text and we will review the address, explain our number and suggest a closing date that fits your move.

faqs.q: Is Manhattan, KS in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The city's floodplain management plan describes flood risk along the Big Blue and Kansas Rivers, and the Manhattan Levee System protects areas of the city. Whether a specific parcel is in a mapped flood zone depends on its address, so check the parcel with the city before you set a price.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Riley County?
faqs.a: December 20 for the first half and May 10 of the following year for the second. If December 20 lands on a weekend, the postmark deadline slides to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental house in Manhattan before I sell it?
faqs.a: The city requires owners to register rental units, and inspections are not part of that program. If the house has been a rental, confirm it is registered so a buyer or title agent does not raise it later.

faqs.q: What is the sales validation questionnaire?
faqs.a: It is a Kansas form that must accompany a deed when it is recorded, unless the transfer is exempt. It records the sale price and conditions for the state's valuation system, and the register of deeds keeps it for five years.

faqs.q: Can I sell a damaged Manhattan house as it is?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners with storm damage, flood damage or deferred repairs can sell without fixing the house first. The trade-off is that an as-is sale is priced for the work the buyer takes on, so compare it with what repairs and a listing would cost you.
